rationale_summary: The guideline is dominantly framed around consumer_public_safety, centering all five statutory duties on protecting human life, physical safety, and property against accidents, operational malfunctions, medical misdiagnoses, critical-infrastructure failures, and adversarial attacks through risk mitigation, safety modes, emergency stops, and victim compensation. Consumer_public_safety edges out fundamental_rights because safety assurance and accident prevention—explicitly contrasted with data-only privacy laws as protecting users' life, body, and property across nuclear, water, energy, transport, and medical systems—drive the document's operational controls and human-oversight architecture. Fundamental_rights is a very close runner-up, co-anchored in the statutory threshold ('life, physical safety, and fundamental rights') and pervading explainability, anti-discrimination/recruitment fairness, user objection/review rights, and personal-data protection. Innovation_enablement is a major third frame emphasizing voluntary flexibility, avoiding duplicate regulation via developer-to-user compliance inheritance and equivalence statements, trade-secret exclusions, and enabling legal-burden-free experimentation. Economic_competitiveness plays a clear supporting role in preparing domestic AI operators for global regulatory regimes (such as the EU AI Act) and strengthening international competitiveness.
